packs.title: Hills & Harbour
packs.promise: Follow the hill, working streets, garden and shore through five separate outings.

q.s: Connect three kinds of evidence inside the fort museum.
st: On an ordinary Tuesday to Friday, start at Sindicat stop 6 around 09:15. Use a valid current ticket for EMT 1 to Dique Oest 23. Allow 36–45 minutes riding and up to 20 minutes waiting. Locate the marked public visitor footway by the terminal, then follow the museum’s signed parking and visitor approach: estimated 340 m with shared driveways and a controlled gate, allowing 10–15 minutes for approach and entry. Stay out of military side roads; if the visitor gate is closed, reschedule. Before entering the museum, obtain valid applicable admission: €5 general, free Wednesdays or documented eligibility. Use the ticket office for discounts and confirm the applicable child rate there.

In currently admitted areas, find a uniform detail, a visible fort feature and a display label that supplies context. Identify each with enough location information to find it again; do not assume any particular object is permanently on display.
Write one sentence linking each observation to a different question: how a person was equipped, how the building worked, and what the museum says about time or place. Mark any inference as your own.

Leave well before 14:00 and retrace the ordinary visitor approach. Find terminal 23 for bus 1 back to Sindicat 6; allow 30–40 minutes riding, waiting, rest and a 20–30 minute reserve. The complete outing takes about 3¼–4¾ hours. No walk onward to Marivent is part of this plan.

q.s: Turn a museum visit into an original small composition.
st: Arrive from Marivent by the signed public Saridakis approach, estimated 530 m uphill with 15–20 minutes allowed, plus 10–15 minutes for admission. Keep the full two-hour visit. Current buses 46 and 47 are diverted via Portopí because of the Saridakis viaduct works; do not follow their old direct-museum route or enter a closed road. Check current visitor notices, concession proof and photography or bag instructions at entry.

In currently admitted spaces, find three spatial relationships: a line meeting an edge, a cluster beside open space, and a change of scale. Record where each appears. You may use building or garden forms; no specific artwork, studio room or current inventory is required.

After observing, make your own six-mark composition in a notebook or written description. Reuse the three relationships rather than copying a displayed work. Explain one change you made to make the composition your own.

Exit by the main visitor entrance and allow 15–20 minutes for the roughly 500 m downhill street corridor to the Joan Miró and Saridakis signals. Find the current signed return stop 91 near that junction, not an old western stop marker. Allow waiting and 35–50 minutes for the return ride, plus rest and reserve in the complete 5½–7¼ hour garden-and-museum outing.

q.s: Compare shore shapes from the dry public promenade.
st: Choose a daylight, calm-weather visit. From the currently permitted public pavement use the marked crossing and the walking side of the shore path. Stop on dry public promenade paving by Vicari Joaquim Fuster, without stepping onto the beach or obstructing cyclists.

Find three different edge shapes visible from public ground: one broad curve, one straight or repeated constructed line, and one small irregular edge. Locate each in words instead of needing a particular boat or business to be present.

Draw a three-line edge map or write a description that puts the shapes in relation. Explain which line seems to hold movement and which opens toward the water; keep interpretations separate from visible facts.

Allow 8–12 minutes for the roughly 300 m public-path return to the Llucmajor signals, then five minutes to locate current bus 35 return stop 447. Use the actual signal and stop signs, a valid ticket and the whole outing’s waiting, ride, rest and 20–30 minute reserve.

packs.title: Old Town Details
packs.promise: Read the Old Town through a market, rooms, stone, light and a living tree.

q.s: Find the evidence that distinguishes three kinds of fresh food.
st: Enter through an ordinary open market door and follow current customer-area signs. Visit before 14:30 on the planned Tuesday to Friday. Choose an aisle position that does not block a transaction, delivery or accessible route.

Find three different fresh-food categories currently represented in open stalls. For each, record one visible feature that distinguishes it, such as a form, storage arrangement or non-personal category label; do not need a particular species or product.
Write three short entries pairing category and feature, then one sentence about how the categories differ. No purchase, tasting, staff interview or photographing vendors is necessary.

Exit to the Sant Miquel public approach and allow 10–15 minutes for the estimated 280 m pedestrian link to Plaça Major. The market part of the proposed 12:15-start plan finishes at about 13:20, leaving time before full trading ends.

q.s: Use an admitted room to plan an original space.
st: At Unió 3 use the currently open signed entrance for Can Balaguer’s free ordinary permanent exhibition. Check the venue programme and staff instructions. Allow 10–15 minutes for finding and entry; a guided-tour reservation, private courtyard or closed room is not part of the task.

In an admitted room, record three located relationships: an opening and the space it serves, a repeated line, and an object’s position relative to a wall or passage. Do not touch furniture, sit on an exhibit or assume a fixed object remains on display.

Draw a small original room plan or describe one in words using those relationships. Change at least one arrangement and explain what your new space would make easier or more noticeable. Make the response from your own observations, not a tracing of a displayed plan.

After the visit and rest, exit to Unió and retrace the earlier permitted public route through Mercat, Weyler, the public stairs, Major and Sant Miquel to Porta Pintada. The combined estimated return is about 860 m with 25–35 minutes allowed, plus exit finding. Allow 20–30 minutes reserve in the complete 4¼–5 hour northern afternoon.

q.s: Connect three details during the ordinary ground-level visit.
st: Use valid BASIC admission for an available window around 13:00 consistent with the 11:30 Ses Voltes start; enter via Museo Catedral at Plaça de la Seu and validate within the booked window. Allow 15 minutes for ticket check and security plus 15 for the slot. Dress respectfully for the temple; no bulky bags or travel cases and no lockers. Pets are excluded except guide dogs; no food or drink except water, and no smoking. Follow any worship or event controls.

In currently admitted ground-level spaces, find one detail that directs light, one that supports or divides space, and one that changes how you see a surface. Record each location without climbing, crossing a barrier or needing a particular artwork.

Write three short observations and one connection between light and structure. Distinguish visible facts from your own interpretation. Use notes rather than assuming a right to photograph works or worshippers.

Allow 10 minutes to exit to the Almoina public street and 10–15 for the estimated 380 m living-street route through Deganat, Sant Roc, Capiscolat, Sant Pere Nolasc, Puresa and Can Serra. Confirm the Banys Àrabs’ current posted admission before entering; its door and queue have a separate allowance.
